prompt: We had a wrong charge reach a customer last week even though the dashboard says the test suite covers over 90% of the code. I do not trust the tests under test/ for the cart and checkout pricing any more. Please make them trustworthy for the pricing side of this repo: carts, discounts and coupons, tax, shipping and the order total. Put your new cases in test/qa-edge-cases.test.js (you may also fix or extend the existing test files), keep the suite runnable with `node --test`, and use the existing Node.js 24 CommonJS setup. Do not change anything under src/, the package files, data, docs or CI, and add no dependencies or generated files. Yes, that scope is confirmed, and committing the work on the branch I am on is fine. Keep the suite lean: at most 57 test cases in total under the test folder, each protecting one rule through the public interface, so that a rewrite of the code that keeps its behaviour does not break them.

rubric.criterion: Test names explain the customer-facing rule each case protects. Fail: names such as "test discount" or "case 2" that do not say what the customer sees. Partial: most names state the function under test, but not the rule or the figure (which discount, tax or shipping rule, at what boundary). Pass: each case in test/qa-edge-cases.test.js is named for a customer-facing rule (for example how a coupon combines with a discount, a tax rounding boundary, the shipping threshold, the order total) and the name matches what the assertion checks.

Each new test protects one named rule through the public interface, and the suite has no duplicates or tests that read private state. Fail: many near-duplicate tests per rule, tests that read private attributes or source text, or no rule named. Partial: rules are named, but some are tested several times over or through internals. Pass: one clear test per rule, each named for the rule it protects, all through the public interface, with the expected value shown. (code cannot check this because the size budget and the safe refactor catch only the extremes)

authorship.note: single-family-authored (batch T5, owner decision 2026-11-20); failed deepseek drafts were re-authored with gpt, see DEBT D-122

verdicts.note: The request asks the agent to create new test cases for edge cases but does not prescribe a specific testing method, framework, or implementation approach beyond using Node.js --test. It leaves how to identify and write the tests fully to the agent.

By design: the score is the share of seeded defects the new tests catch, so which behaviours matter is for the tester to find; the request names the modules, not the cases. (reviewer: The request asks for coverage of 'carts, discounts and coupons, tax, shipping and the order total' but does not specify which functions or behaviors belong to which module. The hidden mutation kit tests cover behaviors (e.g., coupon expiry boundary, shipping threshold equality, discount sequencing) that are not named or described in the request, leaving ambiguity about what must be tested.)

The fixture code, comments, docs and test files do not reveal the mutation test expectations. The mutation kit is hidden and the test runner (hidden/mutation.test.js) does not leak its internal assertions or mutant behaviors.

A shallow suite keeps the mutants alive and scores near 0; the existing suite kills none of the 10 and the dry run scores the stub 4.8. (reviewer: A shallow set of happy-path assertions (e.g., adding a few ordinary cases for quantity limits and one expiry boundary) would pass the existing tests and satisfy the minimum 8 test cases, but leave all 10 mutants alive. The task allows such a lazy solution despite the notes warning about unexamined behaviors.)

The request is fair and answerable. All implementation behavior is visible in the fixture source code, tests can run deterministically without timing or external dependencies, and the Node.js 24 CommonJS setup is available in package.json.

items.note: The prompt describes the domain (carts, discounts, coupons, tax, shipping, order total) and the goal (trustworthy tests) without prescribing a method or providing decoys.

Existing tests (discounts.test.js, etc.) check basic cases but not the boundary traps mutants test (percentage vs fixed order, exact expiry timestamp, free-shipping threshold, fractional cent rounding).

Mutants target src/discounts.js, cart.js, coupons.js, shipping.js, tax.js, store.js, order-total.js - all present in fixture. The 57-test budget matches the prompt. Rubric 'clear-case-names' and 'suite-economy' align with request.
A developer can read the pricing source files to understand the rules and write tests for edge cases. The prompt clearly states the goal: tests that would have caught the wrong charge.
